referee_verbatim: Mouse chromosomes are acro/telocentric with essentially no short arm, so a 1 Mb telomere-anchored 'p-arm' flank is largely composed of minor and major satellite, which are near-identical between chromosomes, placing these windows at once at the top of the Jaccard axis and at the maximum of the multi-mapping problem.

satellite_annotation.label: major satellite GSAT_MM = Dfam-curated ANNOTATION; minor satellite = PROXY (no Dfam 3.8 family named 'minor satellite' for Mus in this library; MurSAT1+MMSAT4+CENSAT_MC used instead); periodicity detector = PROXY
satellite_annotation.hit_filters: blastn length>=100 bp, identity>=75%; bin covered if >=50%

sequence_axis.description: arm-level sequence-sharing Jaccard re-derived from the wfmash all-vs-all PAFs (>=95% identity blocks intersected with the called PHR regions), unmasked and with >=50%-satellite 5 kb bins removed

not_established: contact axis is NOT satellite-masked here: re-masking contacts needs the zuo2021_<stage>.mcool per-bin matrices (h5py/cooler absent from system python; 0.3-0.5 Gpixel per stage) plus the paternal/maternal haplotype mapping

no full RepeatMasker run was possible (RepeatMasker 4.1.7p1 is missing PubRef.pm/FastaDB.pm on this box); only the curated Dfam satellite consensus sequences were used, so non-satellite repeat content is unmeasured

the published arm-level Jaccard is an odgi pangenome-graph node Jaccard and cannot be recomputed with satellite bins excluded without rebuilding the pggb graph; the masked-axis result uses the re-derived PAF-based Jaccard instead
